newsitem.title: USA: MOTOROLA WINS $50 MLN CONTRACT IN POLAND.
newsitem.headline: MOTOROLA WINS $50 MLN CONTRACT IN POLAND.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Tuesday its Cellular Infrastructure Group (CIG) has been awarded a contract valued at $50 million by Poland's Telekomunikacja Polska S.A (TPSA) to build a cellular network.

The network will be the world's largest, and Europe's first, fixed and mobile services network using Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) on Motorola's WiLL wireless local loop system. Commercial service is scheduled to begin in September 1997.

The contract from Telekomunikacja Polska, a government run telephone company in Poland, covers creation of infrastructure which will provide fixed telephone service and mobile or cellular telephone service.
This is the second CDMA WiLL announcement made by Motorola CIG in as many days. On Monday, Motorola said it had been selected to install a $50 million CDMA WiLL network in India.

By combining the cellular features of CDMA with the advantages of wireless local loop technology, up to 100,000 people in Poland will have a choice of either a fixed wireless connection to the home or the office or a limited mobility communications service using conventional CDMA personal phones.

"Motorola's CDMA solution will assist TPSA in meeting the objectives of the national telecommunications program by providing cost-effective, high quality wireless connections throughout Poland," said Paul Strzelecki, vice president and general manager for Motorola CIG's European Cellular Infrastructure Division.

Once the existing waiting list for telephone services has been cleared, the TPSA expects that new applications will be processed virtually instantly and the time between submission of the application and the start of customer service will be reduced to a matter of hours, Motorola said in a news release.
